approachQuestion.prompt:
A chain of sorted samples

A read-only singly linked list contains n integers in nondecreasing order. Only head, n, and next pointers are supplied; there is no index or skip structure. Return whether x occurs. 0 <= n <= 200000. Examples: chain 1->4->9, x=4 -> true; x=6 -> false. Minimize worst-case time, then memory.
constraints: Use only the stated input ordering and access guarantees.

options.text: Walk from head until reaching x, a value greater than x, or the end.
options.feedback: Sorted order permits early termination, but cannot supply constant-time midpoint access through next pointers.

options.text: Copy all values into a random-access array, then binary-search for x.
options.feedback: The copy preserves correctness but still traverses the list and adds avoidable linear storage for this single query.

options.text: Access the midpoint by following next from head, then report absent immediately if it is not equal to x.
options.feedback: For 1->4->9 and x=1, midpoint 4 is unequal although the head matches.

feedback.reason: Walk from head until reaching x, a value greater than x, or the end. Sorted order permits early termination, but cannot supply constant-time midpoint access through next pointers.
details: Walk from head until reaching x, a value greater than x, or the end. Sorted order permits early termination, but cannot supply constant-time midpoint access through next pointers.
A linked list has no constant-time midpoint access. Sortedness lets a forward walk stop above x but does not make node jumps free. An absent value beyond the tail forces traversal of every node.
“Walk from head until reaching x, a value greater than x, or the end.”: Sorted order permits early termination, but cannot supply constant-time midpoint access through next pointers.
“Copy all values into a random-access array, then binary-search for x.”: The copy preserves correctness but still traverses the list and adds avoidable linear storage for this single query.
“Access the midpoint by following next from head, then report absent immediately if it is not equal to x.”: For 1->4->9 and x=1, midpoint 4 is unequal although the head matches.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For target-method, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Analyze only the forward walk. Each pointer step and comparison costs constant time; no index construction, copying, hashing, or recursion. Input storage and returned result storage are excluded; all temporary buffers and call stacks are included.
constraints: Use worst-case bounds. Count all working memory including any stack; exclude supplied inputs and the scalar result.

feedback.reason: Worst-case pointer traversal is linear, with no index or recursion storage.
details: An absent target above every node forces n next-pointer steps and comparisons. Sortedness can shorten some searches but not this worst case. The current pointer and target are constant-size state, with no midpoint index or recursion stack.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Sorted order permits early termination, but cannot supply constant-time midpoint access through next pointers.
“O(n*n + 1) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space”: The fixed method walks next pointers once, with neither pairwise traversal nor a newly built random-access index.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A target after the last node, or absent above all values, forces n link visits.
